focus: Angle 10 failure modes: ungated child sessions in the advisor path, existing over-trigger and default_target guards, the brief-command-advisor cycle, budget headroom, dormant delivery, and ownerMode dead references
noveltyJustification: All 8 findings are new, and the child-session asymmetry plus the doctor-tune cycle are first-time evidence in the packet.
keyQuestions: What prior art exists for routing free text to a packaged workflow, and which failure modes (over-trigger, command/skill ambiguity, child sessions starting commands, loops, brief budget) must a design guard against?
answeredQuestions: What prior art exists for routing free text to a packaged workflow, and which failure modes (over-trigger, command/skill ambiguity, child sessions starting commands, loops, brief budget) must a design guard against?
ruledOut: A separate command loop-breaker subsystem: the cycle is one command calling the advisor so a depth counter at the brief boundary suffices
Relying on the ambiguity brief form for command ties: it takes two skill labels and has no slot for a command string

graphEvents.label: Which failure modes must a command-surfacing design guard against
Advisor path lacks the child-session gate Gate 3 has
A brief-to-command rule creates a command-advisor cycle

label: Child sessions are ungated in the advisor path: the spec gate implements AI_SESSION_CHILD with isChildSession and makes Gate 3 a no-op for a dispatched child, but the advisor hook library and Claude adapter carry no equivalent check, so a dispatched child still receives briefs and a run-on-brief rule would let a child start commands by itself.

Over-triggering already has two guards: keepPassingSkillsAboveDoctorBridges demotes a doctor bridge below any passing skill unless a lead phrase matches, and the deriver rejects a lead_phrase absent from trigger_phrases; both are doctor-only today.

Bare-command recall is bounded by design: default_target is allowed at most once per command, only on a multi-target command and never on a mutating route, which is the existing precedent for one safe entry point per command.

Ambiguity is first-class but skill-shaped: ambiguousWith, heldBelow and a 120-token ambiguous brief form exist, and the baseline scores ambiguity top-1 at 20 of 24 with tau 0.03, but no part of that machinery mentions commands.

A brief-to-command rule creates a real cycle: /doctor:skill-advisor tune itself runs advisor_recommend and advisor_validate, so a brief that can cause a command run plus a command that calls the advisor is cyclic and nothing in the hooks counts depth or suppresses re-entry.

The budget is headroom rather than cap: the routing head is capped at 80 tokens (120 ambiguous) with the 218-character directive outside the cap, so one added command-and-policy clause fits in the existing 320-character head budget.

Dormant delivery turns a rule into a dead letter: Cursor documents its dynamic adapter as dormant and routes from a static rule, so any instruction conditioned on the brief naming a command does nothing on Cursor and Devin and needs an explicit no-brief branch that asks the advisor directly.

Dangling linkage is checked for ids but not owners: the bridge-resolution guard sweeps slash ids for dead commands while nothing checks ownerMode, leaving sk-create-skill-parent without a SKILL.md, /memory:save and /spec_kit without a command file, and 18 doctor bridges without a benchmark row as three uncovered dead-reference classes.
Any rule that starts a command from a brief must be gated on AI_SESSION_CHILD and on brief-reentry depth, because neither guard exists in the advisor path today
